basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 17.' and it opens 'Vers. 17. Et in uno canistro, quod erat excelsius, portare me omnes cibos, qui fiunt arte'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 17. Et in uno canistro, quod erat excelsius, portare me omnes cibos, qui fiunt arte pistoria. In Graeco habetur, portare me chondriton, id est panem cibarium. Sed hoc non convenit Pharaoni, ut cibario pane vesceretur. Potuit tamen fieri, ut beatus Augustinus dicit, ut canistra videretur habere deorsum panes cibarios, supra quos erant omnia, quae fiunt arte pistoria. Mystice hi duo viri duo sunt populi, qui ambo graviter peccaverunt, ut Apostolus dicit: Non est distinctio Judaei et Graeci, | Omnes peccaverunt et egent gloria Dei (Rom. X, 12). Sed apparente vero Joseph, alter, id est Judaicus, non credendo in ligno crucis damnatus est, in ligno praevaricationis.
